title: Dedicated GPU pool degradation — SRE ops notes and runbook draft
body:
Summary:

This is a working postmortem / runbook draft capturing the November 2025 GPU-pool degradation incident affecting Dedicated capacity customers. Impact window ~2025-11-07 03:12 UTC -> 2025-11-07 06:40 UTC (user-visible error rate + tail latency spikes). Primary symptoms: queued requests, token-generation latency increasing 5x, occasional OOMs on a small subset of pods.

Why this doc exists (context):
- Rapidly capture what we observed, immediate mitigations, and concrete runbook steps for on-call.
- Draft follow-ups for Platform/Serving and Dedicated product teams (autoscaling config, isolation settings).
- Record unknowns for later RCA.

Quick timeline (local times in UTC):
- 03:12 — First alert: host-level GPU memory pressure alert from Prometheus (alert: GPU_Mem_Used_pct > 92% for 3m) on pool-dedicated-prod-us-west-2-a.
- 03:19 — Increased request queuing in front of model router (observed queue depth spike to ~400 requests).
- 03:24 — Pager routed to SRE on-call. Initial message shows elevated 95th/99th latency for generation route (/v1/generate).
- 03:30 — On-call ran quick inventory (kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -l pool=dedicated-usw2) and spotted several pods with GPU util 100% and persistent CUDA OOM logs.
- 03:45 — Mitigation: cordon + drain one suspected noisy node, evict high-usage pods, scale up temporary GPU nodes (manual + cloud provider API) to relieve queueing.
- 04:05 — Latency started to improve but then flared again 04:35 — observed autoscaler failed to add nodes due to label mismatch (autoscaler looking for nodeGroup=dedicated-gpu, but nodes provisioned with node_group=dedicated-gpu).
- 04:40 — Manual fix: hand-created nodes with correct label and forced cluster-autoscaler sync. Queue drained by 05:10.
- 06:40 — Customer traffic back to normal; incident declared mitigated.

Immediate root-cause hypothesis (short):
1) A combination of a noisy neighbor workload (single pod with runaway attention-length causing excessive KV cache growth + repeated retry loops causing GPU mem pressure) and
2) Autoscaler config mismatch (label typo) that prevented automated scaling from responding in time, increasing duration of degradation.

Evidence collected:
- Pod logs: repeated "CUDA out of memory" and long sequences of large context tokenization ("context_len=24512" shown in logs). Pod ID: model-runner-7d9cf (node ip 10.12.5.23).
- Metrics: GPU_mem_used_pct peaked at 99.2% on 3 nodes. Scheduler queue depth metric (model_router_queue) correlated strongly with GPU mem alerts.
- Autoscaler logs: rejected scale-up because node group selector did not match labels on newly-provisioned instances. Error snippet: "node group selector mismatch: expected label nodeGroup=dedicated-gpu". Cloud provisioner created nodes with node_group=dedicated-gpu (underscore vs camelcase).
- Recent change: Serving runtime PR #2145 (linked) added a more permissive pod retry loop for edge timeouts — likely amplified the noisy-pod retries.

Mitigations performed (chronological):
- Cordoned noisy node (kubectl cordon <node>) and evicted pods (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data) to stop immediate noisy neighbor.
- Scaled a temporary nodepool (manual) with correct labels so scheduler could place new replicas.
- Updated cluster-autoscaler config to increase scale-up aggressiveness for GPU pools (temporary); reverted after stabilization.

On-call checklist (immediate actions) — draft runbook steps:
1) Detect + validate:
   - Check alerts: GPU_Mem_Used_pct > 90% persistent; model_router_queue > 100 for 3m.
   - kubectl get nodes -l pool=dedicated-usw2 -o wide; check node GPU metrics with `kubectl top pod -n redwood-serving --containers` or `nvidia-smi` on node.
   - Identify pods with high GPU memory: grep "CUDA out of memory" in logs: `kubectl logs -n redwood-serving <pod> --since=10m | grep -i "out of memory"`
2) Short-term isolation:
   - If a pod is using >85% GPU memory for >= 3 min, mark node as 'noisy' and cordon: `kubectl cordon <node>`.
   - Evict offending pod: `kubectl delete pod <pod> -n redwood-serving --grace-period=30` (we accept that eviction may restart the workload elsewhere; see step 4 for better long-term control).
   - If eviction causes placement back onto the same node repeatedly, taint node: `kubectl taint nodes <node> noisy=true:NoSchedule` and notify infra to inspect node-level GPU driver state.
3) Scale up if queueing is visible:
   - Check cluster-autoscaler status: `kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/cluster-autoscaler` for scale rejection reasons.
   - If autoscaler failed (label mismatch or cloud API delay), create manual nodes with the correct labels using the cloud console/infra tooling and annotate them with `nodeGroup=dedicated-gpu` (match exact string expected by autoscaler).
   - After manual nodes are up, run `kubectl get nodes -l nodeGroup=dedicated-gpu` and confirm scheduler is placing pods.
4) Prevent immediate re-tries that amplify load:
   - If we see runaway retries in pod logs, temporarily block retries by patching the deployment: `kubectl patch deployment <dep> -n redwood-serving --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/gpu","value":"1"}]'` OR adjust the retry env var config to minimal.
   - Consider scaling down replica count for the offending model (not the whole pool) until we can debug the model behavior.
5) Communication:
   - Post a status update in #dedicated-prod (Slack) with current queue depth and ETA. Use template: "SRE investigating GPU pool degradation in usw2. Queues: <n>. Mitigations: cordoned node X, manual nodes addition. ETA 30m."

Diagnostics commands cheat sheet (quick):
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -o wide -l pool=dedicated-usw2
- kubectl logs -n redwood-serving <pod> --since=5m | tail -n 200
- kubectl exec -it <node> -- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
- kubectl describe node <node> | egrep "Taints|Labels|Allocatable|Capacity"
- curl -s "http://model-router-metrics:9090/metrics" | grep model_router_queue

Longer term actions / follow-ups (RCA -> action items):
- P1: Fix autoscaler label mismatch and add unit/integration tests to infra CI that validate node provisioning labels. Owner: Infra team (Carlos). Due: 2026-03-15. (linked issue DED-4021)
- P1: Harden retry logic in serving runtime PRs: ensure exponential backoff + circuit-breaker for long-running context lengths. Owner: Serving-runtime (Ethan). Due: 2026-02-12.
- P2: Add GPU mem headroom alert (alert when per-node mem > 82% for 5m AND model_router_queue > 50) to reduce time-to-detect noisy neighbors. Owner: Observability (Lena). Due: 2026-01-30.
- P2: Implement auto-isolation for nodes: when a node triggers GPU OOM 3x in 15m, auto-taint it and route new pods away for automated investigation. Owner: SRE + Platform. Due: 2026-04-01.
- P3: Create a canary test harness that spins up a synthetic workload that simulates long context lengths and validates autoscaler and routing behavior weekly. Owner: QA/Platform. Due: 2026-03-01.

Draft runbook changes to add (text for PR):
- Add a new section "Noisy GPU isolation" with clear thresholds (GPU_MEM > 85% for 3m -> cordon, 90% 1m -> auto-evict + taint).
- Document exact autoscaler label keys expected (nodeGroup=dedicated-gpu) and change cloud provisioner to set both nodeGroup and node_group in metadata to be defensive.
- Add a rollback checklist for changes in serving runtime that modify retry behavior: quick toggle via feature-flag (FF) to disable new retry loop in production.

Things we still don't know / open questions:
- Why did the cloud provisioner start emitting node_group instead of nodeGroup? Recent infra deploys? (audit logs linked).
- Was there a correlated customer job (large context) that started just before 03:12? Need to query billing/usage logs for large batch job IDs.
- Does the model runner's memory accounting misreport peak usage sometimes (observed mismatch ~5-10% between nvidia-smi and prometheus exporter)? Investigate exporter collector version.

Notes to self / informal snippets (on-call flavor):
- "If you see queue > 200, don't wait for autoscaler to finish 5-min window — add a node manually if infrastructure is slow."
- "When cordoning, leave a sticky Slack message so infra knows not to recycle node until SRE clears it — avoid immediate node replacement causing autoscaler confusion."
- "Watch for PR #2145 — revert or feature-flag if we see repeated incidents after patch deploys."

Follow-up comms plan:
- Short postmortem draft to be shared in #infra-postmortems in 48 hours. Include timeline, root cause hypothesis, and immediate P1 fixes.
- Customer-facing one-pager (CS to own) summarizing impact, remediation, and what we changed. Target: 72 hours.

Appendix: Useful links and quick references:
- Autoscaler config in infra repo: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/terraform/modules/cluster-autoscaler (PR linked above)
- Serving runtime PR: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/2145
- Incident ticket: SRE-887

End of working draft — keep this as the canonical working doc for now. Will convert to formal postmortem after RCA and once follow-ups have owners assigned and committed.

-- Priya (SRE)
